title: Normalized derived comparison for a specified finite free point resolution
statement: For commutative condensed rings Λ,Λ′, a map a:Λ→Λ′, normalized scalar pullback data D, and a short exact point-module complex S with both first terms isomorphic to a specified finite biproduct of r regular Λ-modules and with specified quotient identification t:S.X3≅Res_a Λ′, its pulled-back augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and its cone is K-flat; the native localization tensor comparison is invertible against any complex. There exists a natural beta from tensor by the localized pulled-back cone to restricted derived scalar extension. It satisfies the exact AugmentationNormalized condition, the specified pullback square and the displayed equality between the conjugated actual scalar mate and scalar-first projection. This assertion includes neither projection invertibility nor gamma invertibility.

proof.text: The functor $p_Z^*=\pi_Z^{-1}a^*$ is strong symmetric monoidal, and $a^*$ is exact, by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]; the inverse image $\pi_Z^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Hence $p_Z^*$ is exact. Hence it carries this short exact sequence to $0\to O_Z^r\xrightarrow{\phi_Z}O_Z^r\xrightarrow{q_Z}A_Z\to0$, with the same finite-sum coordinates and action maps. For the passage to section-ring module sheaves use the exact tensor equivalence [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], which preserves finite powers, acyclicity and K-flatness. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-free-mono-cokernel-kflat] to this specified monomorphism and cokernel. It says that the specified augmentation $P_Z\to A_Z[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism, that its terms are flat and that $P_Z$ is K-flat. It also identifies $P_Z$ with the cone of $\phi_Z[0]$, including the augmentation from its degree-zero term.

source.place: Integral-to-finite bullet: pull back the resolution; K-flatness as in Stacks Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat

proof.text: Work with section-ring sheaves via [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] and the derived scalar adjunction equivalence [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. Let $C$ represent $K$ and choose a flat-term K-flat replacement $Q\to C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The native one-K-flat tensor comparison [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] identifies $P_Z\otimes^LK$ with $Q_{O_Z}\operatorname{Tot}(P_Z\otimes C)$ and with $Q_{O_Z}\operatorname{Tot}(P_Z\otimes Q)$. Tensoring the augmentation $P_Z\to A_Z[0]$ with the K-flat $Q$ gives a quasi-isomorphism to $A_Z\otimes Q$; this is preservation of quasi-isomorphisms by tensoring with a fixed K-flat complex in [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs]. In [lem-pe-restricted-kflat-tensor-identification], take its coefficient tower $B\to A\to S$ to be $O_Z\xrightarrow{1}O_Z\xrightarrow{a_Z}A_Z$. Its scalar-first computation identifies $Q_{O_Z}(A_Z\otimes Q)$ with $\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z}T_ZK$. Composing gives the augmentation-induced isomorphism $\beta_{Z,K}:P_Z\otimes^LK\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z}T_ZK$. All arrows are the specified localization/tensor comparisons; the resolving equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes them natural in $K$ and independent of $Q$. In particular we do not claim that $P_Z\otimes C\to A_Z\otimes C$ is a quasi-isomorphism for an arbitrary $C$.

source.place: Integral-to-finite bullet: the actual augmentation-induced ordinary derived tensor model; Stacks Tags 06YS, 06YT

proof.text: For $h:Z'\to Z$, the monoidal composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] identifies $h^{-1}O_Z$ with $O_{Z'}$, $h^{-1}A_Z$ with $A_{Z'}$, and the pulled-back maps $\phi_Z,q_Z$ with $\phi_{Z'},q_{Z'}$. Thus it identifies the augmented complexes themselves. The canonical pullback/scalar comparison is the balancing-arrow comparison on K-flat representatives by [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]; in particular it sends $1\otimes x$ to $1\otimes h^{-1}x$ and needs no flatness of $a$. Choose $Q\to C$ as in step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] (with $c$ the identification $h^{-1}O_Z\cong O_{Z'}$), $h^*Q=h^{-1}Q$ is again K-flat with flat terms, so it is a resolution of $h^*K$ usable in step 4 over $Z'$, and $h^{-1}\operatorname{Tot}(P_Z\otimes Q)=\operatorname{Tot}(h^{-1}P_Z\otimes h^{-1}Q)$ represents the canonical tensor pullback isomorphism $h^*(P_Z\otimes^LK)\cong P_{Z'}\otimes^Lh^*K$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Naturality of tensor with respect to the augmentation makes the square for $h^*\beta_{Z,K}$ and $\beta_{Z',h^*K}$ commute on these representatives, hence in the derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. These are precisely the comparisons of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1). Identity and composite $h$ obey the same square because the cited point-pullback and scalar-comparison statements give their identity and composition coherence.

proof.text: To compare the actual internal-module arrows with ringed-site arrows, use [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] for both condensed rings $\underline O,\underline A$. It identifies their unbounded derived geometric adjunctions, including the counits. Use [lem-pd-section-derived-tensor-normalization] for the actual pullback tensor isomorphism and [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] for derived extension and restriction with their units and counits. Thus it suffices to compute the arrow in section-ring module categories. The hypotheses here are only smallness of the sites and pulled-back coefficients; the monoidal coefficient identifications from the preceding step give the cartesian coefficient square required for [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. That lemma is stated for the adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with $c$ the coefficient identification from the point, while the normalization above lands in the ringed derived pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and K-injective direct image of the section model. These coincide: both inverse images are the same tensor-formula pullback $f^{-1}(-)\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y,c}R_X$ with the same ordinary module adjunction, exact because $c$ is invertible, so derived termwise on every complex; both direct images are computed on K-injective resolutions. Hence both derived adjunctions are the unique canonical bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] induced by that one ordinary adjunction, for $R=O$ and for $R=A$. Write $r_Z=\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z}$ and $d:r_YRf_{*,A}\cong Rf_{*,O}r_X$ for its specified direct-image comparison.

proof.text:
Put $L=f_O^*$, $R=Rf_{*,O}$ and $B=P_Y$, so $LB=P_X$. Let $t=T_X(\varepsilon_K)c_{f,RK}$, the $A$-adjunct defining $\gamma_{f,K}$. The adjunct-compatibility equation of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] says that $d\,r_Y(\gamma)$ is the $O$-adjunct of $r_X(t)b^{-1}$, where $b:r_Xf_A^*\cong Lr_Y$. Under $L\beta_{Y,RK}$, the pullback square in step 5 identifies $r_X(c)b^{-1}L\beta_{Y,RK}$ with $\beta_{X,LRK}$ following the tensor pullback isomorphism $L(B\otimes^LRK)\cong P_X\otimes^LLRK$. Naturality of $\beta$ for $\varepsilon_K:LRK\to K$ now gives
$$r_X(t)b^{-1}L\beta_{Y,RK}=\beta_{X,K}(1_{P_X}\otimes\varepsilon_K)\mu,$$
where $\mu$ is that tensor pullback isomorphism. The normalization of $c$ used here is exactly [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], not a freely chosen isomorphism. By the natural adjunction bijection, the conjugate $R(\beta_{X,K}^{-1})d\,r_Y(\gamma)\beta_{Y,RK}$ is therefore the adjunct of $(1_{P_X}\otimes\varepsilon_K)\mu$. This is the scalar-first projection map in the statement, the symmetric form of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The tensor symmetries and unit comparisons are the canonical ones of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor].
